function: DDPG agent jointly sets BS and UAV beamforming vectors and UAV position to maximize NOMA users' average rate under a sensing CRB limit (p. 1, 4).
system: Downlink C-NOMA: Z-antenna BS (Z not given), full-duplex decode-and-forward UAV relay, 1-antenna receiver BS, 4 single-antenna users, 1 moving target; sub-6 GHz; no RIS (p. 2, 4).
method: DDPG reinforcement learning (actor-critic, target networks, replay buffer); penalty-based reward; beamformer normalization enforces power budgets; trained by interaction over episodes (p. 4).
data_channel: Own simulator: BS-UAV and BS-user channels as in the authors' earlier [5] (Rayleigh, Rician), free-space UAV-user link, LoS sensing links, random-waypoint target (p. 2-3).
test_conditions: Episodes reset channels, beamformers and target location; results averaged over 100 realizations; CRB limit and UAV power are varied; no unseen scenario reported (p. 4-5).
baselines: Traditional UAV trajectory benchmarks (straight line, stationary, optimized stationary); DDPG variants: SDMA model, random initial UAV position; SCA only compared in complexity (p. 1, 4-5).
metrics: Average rate of communication users versus UAV power; average reward per episode; UAV trajectory and achievable rate under CRB limits (Fig. 2) (p. 5).
complexity: Big-O orders: training O(MB(L1(I_mu+I_Q)+2L1L2+L2(U_mu+1))); deployed running time O(WLNe); SCA order given; no measured runtime (p. 4).
openness: none; no code or data link (p. 1-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "follows the same channel models adopted in [5]"; Rayleigh and Rician channels from the authors' earlier paper, free-space UAV-user link, LoS sensing links (p. 2-3); custom simulator, no 3GPP model or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "Finally, the results are averaged over 100 realizations"; CRB limit and UAV power are only swept (Fig. 2b-c), and the paper never tests a trained agent in a new scenario or configuration.
q3_support: p. 4: "The UAV-assisted model is compared with several benchmarks corresponding to different UAV movement strategies"; the DDPG variants (SDMA model, random initial position) are not earlier learned methods, and no other learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "the complexity of the training algorithm can be written as"; training order O(MB(L1(I_mu+I_Q)+2L1L2+L2(U_mu+1))) and deployed running time O(WLNe) are given.
q5_support: p. 5: "Finally, the results are averaged over 100 realizations"; the data come from the authors' own simulation, and no code, dataset link or DOI appears in the letter.
notes: Included as area 6, not 5: the DDPG agent controls beamforming (physical layer) jointly with UAV position on an aerial relay link that also senses (p. 4), and 6 outranks 5 in the tie-break order. The trajectory part is above the physical layer, but the joint beamforming decision passes the above_phy check. q3 is borderline: the Fig. 2(c) benchmarks are UAV movement strategies plus two DDPG variants of the proposed model, read from the legend on the image of page 5, so no earlier learned method is compared; the reviewer should confirm. The text gives no numeric Z, network sizes or learning rates.
